title.es: Un pequeño despachador de servidor MCP

prompt.en:
Write `handle(message, tools)` for a server that offers only tools. `tools` maps a name to `{"description", "inputSchema", "handler"}`, where `handler(arguments)` returns text or raises `ValueError`.

- A message without an `"id"` is a notification: return `None`.
- If `jsonrpc` is not `"2.0"` or `method` is not a string, return error `-32600`.
- `tools/list`: result `{"tools": [{"name", "description", "inputSchema"}, ...]}`, never the handler.
- `tools/call` with `params.name` and `params.arguments`: an unknown tool is protocol error `-32602`. Otherwise run the handler and return result `{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": ...}], "isError": False}`; if it raises `ValueError`, return the same shape with the error message and `"isError": True`.
- Any other method: error `-32601`.

Every response has `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`, the request `id`, and either `result` or `error` (`{"code", "message"}`).
prompt.es:
Escribe `handle(message, tools)` para un servidor que solo ofrece herramientas. `tools` asocia un nombre a `{"description", "inputSchema", "handler"}`, donde `handler(arguments)` devuelve texto o lanza `ValueError`.

- Un mensaje sin `"id"` es una notificación: devuelve `None`.
- Si `jsonrpc` no es `"2.0"` o `method` no es un texto, devuelve el error `-32600`.
- `tools/list`: resultado `{"tools": [{"name", "description", "inputSchema"}, ...]}`, nunca el handler.
- `tools/call` con `params.name` y `params.arguments`: una herramienta desconocida es el error de protocolo `-32602`. Si no, ejecuta el handler y devuelve el resultado `{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": ...}], "isError": False}`; si lanza `ValueError`, devuelve la misma forma con el mensaje de error e `"isError": True`.
- Cualquier otro método: error `-32601`.

Toda respuesta lleva `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`, el `id` de la petición y `result` o `error` (`{"code", "message"}`).

tests:
def get_order(args):
    if "order_id" not in args:
        raise ValueError("order_id is required")
    return "order " + args["order_id"] + ": shipped"
schema = {"type": "object", "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["order_id"]}
tools = {"get_order": {"description": "Look up an order", "inputSchema": schema, "handler": get_order}}
listed = handle({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list"}, tools)
assert listed["jsonrpc"] == "2.0" and listed["id"] == 1, "a response echoes jsonrpc 2.0 and the request id"
assert listed["result"]["tools"] == [{"name": "get_order", "description": "Look up an order", "inputSchema": schema}], "tools/list returns name, description and inputSchema, never the handler"
ok = handle({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "get_order", "arguments": {"order_id": "A7"}}}, tools)
assert ok["result"] == {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "order A7: shipped"}], "isError": False}, "a successful call returns text content with isError false"
bad = handle({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "get_order", "arguments": {}}}, tools)
assert bad["result"]["isError"] is True and "order_id" in bad["result"]["content"][0]["text"], "bad arguments are a tool execution error: a normal result with isError true and a readable message"
unknown = handle({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 4, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "drop_db", "arguments": {}}}, tools)
assert unknown["error"]["code"] == -32602 and "result" not in unknown, "an unknown tool is a protocol error (-32602), not a result"
assert handle({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "method": "prompts/list"}, tools)["error"]["code"] == -32601, "a method the server does not offer is -32601"
assert handle({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"}, tools) is None, "a notification has no id and gets no response"
assert handle({"id": 6, "method": "tools/list"}, tools)["error"]["code"] == -32600, "a message without jsonrpc 2.0 is an invalid request"

hint.en: Write two small helpers, `ok(id, result)` and `err(id, code, message)`, that build the response dicts. Then the function is a short chain of `if` checks in the order of the bullet list.
hint.es: Escribe dos pequeñas funciones, `ok(id, result)` y `err(id, code, message)`, que construyan los dicts de respuesta. Así la función queda como una corta cadena de `if` en el orden de la lista.
